content.text:
The simplified text reads fine, but it now disagrees with the commit in three places, so one side has to change.

1. **`vc-x1 sync` is not what the instructions name.** The Problem says the agent-files mention "fetching using `vc-x1 sync`". They don't: Acquaint names `jj git fetch -R .` and `jj git fetch -R <agent-dir>`, and no agent-file mentions `vc-x1 sync` at all. The new Opening step follows Acquaint, so it also uses `jj git fetch`.
   - The difference matters: `jj git fetch` only looks, while `vc-x1 sync` also moves the local bookmark to the remote's and can rebase `@`. Acquaint's rule today is "report and leave as found".
   - If you want the rule to be `vc-x1 sync`, that is a change to both Acquaint and Opening, and I'd want your word on whether syncing without asking is intended.

2. **"Hasn't been synced in a while" is not in the rule.** The Solution says to sync at every cycle start "or if a repo hasn't been synced in a while", and the Problem says "or even more often". The Opening step I wrote only covers cycle starts.
   - To put it in the rule it needs a trigger an agent can check; "a while" is not one. Candidates are "before any push" or "when the last fetch was in an earlier session".
   - Otherwise I'd drop both phrases from the block.

3. **The messages repo is gone from the Solution.** The commit still adds the messages fetch to `custom.md`, and the acceptance check tests it. A clause would cover it: "and `custom.md` adds the messages repo's fetch at the same moments."

Two small wording points: "instructions ... mentions" should be "mention", and "it should be synced" reads more plainly as "is synced".

Which way do you want 1 and 2 to go? My recommendation is to keep `jj git fetch` and cycle starts only for this baby step, and correct the block's text to match: say "fetching" without naming `vc-x1 sync`, drop "in a while" and "even more often", and add the `custom.md` clause. On your word I'll make whichever edits you choose and revalidate.

content.content:
vc-x1 0.84.20

Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.

Repo set is resolved (in order):
  - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)
  - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`
  - neither             `.`, the one repo sync is run in

One atomic operation: fetch, then per repo:
  - up-to-date        nothing to do
  - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote
  - ahead             nothing to sync (local has unpushed work)
  - diverged          rebase local onto remote; fail on conflicts
  - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip

After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
bookmark: the work repo `jj new`s a clean `@` (or rebases a
dirty one with --rebase / a prompt), the `.claude` session
repo `jj new main`s when main moved (no-op when `@-` is
already the main tip).

On failure sync stops where the failing step stopped: nothing
is auto-reverted, so the state can be inspected. The failure
report prints each repo's pre-sync op id; undo explicitly with
`jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing persists across
invocations.

Output shape:
  - all-up-to-date: one-line summary (`sync: N repos are up to date, nothing to
  sync`)
  - action needed:  per-repo fetch + state + actions
  - --quiet:        no output; exit code signals success

Usage: vc-x1 sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -q, --quiet
          Suppress all informational output (exit code signals result)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to sync in the work repo. The session (bot) repo is a linear
          journal and always syncs `main`, regardless
          
          [default: main]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --remote <REMOTE>
          Remote to sync against
          
          [default: origin]

      --rebase
          Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without asking.
          
          After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced bookmark.
          When the work repo's `@` carries changes it normally asks before
          rebasing, and `--rebase` answers yes up front for non-interactive use.
          Ignored for the bot repo (which always `jj new main`).

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>

vc-x1 0.84.20

Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.

Repo set is resolved (in order):
  - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)
  - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`
  - neither             `.`, the one repo sync is run in

One atomic operation: fetch, then per repo:
  - up-to-date        nothing to do
  - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote
  - ahead             nothing to sync (local has unpushed work)
  - diverged          rebase local onto remote; fail on conflicts
  - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip

After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
bookmark: the work repo `jj new`s a clean `@` (or rebases a
dirty one with --rebase / a prompt), the `.claude` session
repo `jj new main`s when main moved (no-op when `@-` is
already the main tip).

On failure sync stops where the failing step stopped: nothing
is auto-reverted, so the state can be inspected. The failure
report prints each repo's pre-sync op id; undo explicitly with
`jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing persists across
invocations.

**Messages references:** the set is clean. `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*` contain no reference to `vc-x1-messages` or a messages repo. The only ones are in `custom.md`, the project layer: the existing Messaging pointer on line 11, and the Fetch sub-bullet I added under it in this cycle. (`rationale.md` mentions "the family's messaging rules" once, as history of a retired file.)

So I read your "no" as: keep the messages fetch out of the cycle's Solution and out of the set. One thing to confirm: do you want the new `custom.md` sub-bullet kept, or removed too? I'd keep it, since `custom.md` is exactly the place for a this-family-only rule and you asked for the fetch earlier, and just not mention it in the Solution.

**Using `vc-x1 sync`:** I'll switch both Acquaint and Opening to `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, run from the workspace root. I read the code to see what that changes, because sync acts where `jj git fetch` only looks:

| State of `main` | `jj git fetch` today | `vc-x1 sync` |
|---|---|---|
| Up to date | nothing | nothing |
| Behind | reported, left as found | fast-forwarded, a clean `@` moved onto it |
| Ahead | reported | reported, nothing done |
| Diverged | reported, left as found | local `main` rebased onto the remote's, fails on conflicts |

- **Mid-cycle it is safe:** when `@` sits on a cycle bookmark ahead of `main`, sync leaves `@` in place. A non-empty `@` is also left in place, since the agent has no terminal to answer the rebase prompt.
- **It conflicts with one sentence in Acquaint:** "Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until the user says how to proceed." Behind and diverged would now be acted on first and reported after.

My proposed wording for the rule: the session runs `vc-x1 sync --scope=both` and reports what it printed; behind is fast-forwarded by the sync, ahead is a finding, and a sync that rebased or failed is a finding the acquaint stops on. The cycle bookmark, when one is in flight, is still compared by looking, not synced.

Two answers and I'll make the edits, fix the block's text to match, and revalidate:
1. Keep or remove the `custom.md` messages-fetch sub-bullet?
2. Is an automatic rebase of a diverged `main` acceptable at acquaint and cycle start, or should diverged stay "report and stop"? Sync has no look-only mode, so "report and stop" would mean a `jj git fetch` look first and a sync only when behind.

  Passed.

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

## Counts

| Landed | Cycle | Files | Lines | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-25 | docs: the family agent-files proposal opening | 10 | 2205 | vc-x1's set |
| 2026-08-27 | docs: sync the agent-files to zc-ring-x1's set | 12 | 2822 | two files back, 863 |
| 2026-08-28 | docs: the family agent-files proposal | 11 | 2126 | cycle-checklists and cycle-protocol folded into AGENTS.md, commit-model added |
| 2026-08-31 | docs: point custom.md at the messages repo | 11 | 2127 | the messaging line replaces custom.md's `_None._` |
| 2026-08-31 | agent-files(adoption): from iiac-perf, zc-ring-x1, 2026-08-31 | 10 | 2109 | iiac-perf's set verbatim, messaging.md out |
| 2026-08-31 | agent-files(proposal): to iiac-perf, zc-ring-x1, 2026-08-31 | 10 | 2158 | the commit-vocabulary section and its rationale, declared types in |
| 2026-09-01 | agent-files(proposal): v0.1.0 | 10 | 2230 | the set's version and its rationale, titles by version, the empty version file uncounted |
| 2026-09-04 | agent-files(adoption): v0.2.0 | 10 | 2231 | iiac-perf's set verbatim: `## Closed` last in the Todo format list, `# References` named, the re-pack parenthetical dropped |
| 2026-09-04 | agent-files(proposal): v0.2.1 | 10 | 2238 | the agent-repo's directory comes from `.vc-config.md` at six sites, and the `ochid:` trailer's `/.claude` says at first use that it is a label and not one |
| 2026-09-04 | agent-files(proposal): v0.2.2 | 10 | 2255 | iiac-perf's notes on v0.2.1 plus wink's: the citation names the work-repo's config, the label rule keeps one home, the `[repos]` specimen says which cell the project chooses, and the `ochid:` prefix names a side rather than a path, and both repos are located by the `[repos]` entry that resolves home rather than by a literal directory |
| 2026-09-07 | agent-files(adoption): v0.2.3 | 10 | 2315 | iiac-perf's set verbatim by `vc-x1 agent-files copy`: eight rules corrected where they live with a why each in `rationale.md`, the dual-repo model as two definitions, the agent-files version tending to the patch, and the heading and term renamed "Agent-files version" |
| 2026-09-11 | agent-files(proposal): v0.2.4 | 10 | 2315 | the messaging pointer in `custom.md` names Pending instead of an inbox, one clause reworded on one line, so the count holds |
| 2026-09-16 | agent-files(adoption): v0.2.5 | 9 | 1774 | zc-ring-x1's proposal verbatim: a size row only when an agent-file changed, with its why, and `rationale.md` out of the count, so the files drop to 9 and the total loses its 543 lines |

content.text:
Agreed, sync should have a look-only mode. That is code, though, so it is a separate piece of work from this agent-files cycle, and you pick how it enters.

**Where the cycle stands now:** before your message arrived I had already switched both rules to `vc-x1 sync --scope=both` as you asked, and validation passes on that state.
- **Acquaint:** the Not level check runs the sync and reports what it prints; a fast-forward, a rebase, and an ahead `main` are each a finding. A cycle bookmark in flight is still only compared, never synced.
- **Opening:** the new first step is Sync, ahead of the bookmark.
- **Rationale and block:** updated to match, with your Problem and Solution text corrected to say the old rule was a `jj git fetch` and to drop "in a while", which no rule backs.
- **`custom.md`:** the messages pointer and its Fetch sub-bullet are kept, and the set itself names no messages repo.

**Options for the look-only mode:**
1. **Land v0.2.8 as it stands, and add a Todo entry for the mode (my recommendation).** The entry goes first in `## Todo` as `feat: sync has a look-only mode`. When it lands, a one-line agent-files change points Acquaint and Opening at it. Until then a behind `main` is fast-forwarded and a diverged one rebased at acquaint, both reported.
2. **Build the mode first.** Set this cycle aside, run the `feat` as its own cycle, then finish v0.2.8 against the new flag. The rules are never written in the acting form, but it is two more round trips before anything lands.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

feat: bare sync acts on the repo it is run in

A bare sync, `vc-x1 sync` with neither -R nor --scope, can be read two
ways. One reading is "sync the repo I am in", which is what chid, desc,
list, and show do with no flags. The other is "sync the workspace I am

took the second, so a user holding the first synced a repo they had
not named.

    so from a subdirectory of a repo it fails and changes nothing.
  - Both repos are asked for with --scope=both, from anywhere in the
    workspace.
* Sync resolved its flags by code of its own.
  - It calls the resolver the four read commands use, so the five
    cannot drift apart.

current directory, where it synced both repos of a dual workspace.

content.text:
Delaying makes sense to me. It avoids writing the acting form of the rule now and rewriting it a cycle later.

**On the delay**
- **What gets parked:** the v0.2.8 working copy is unpushed, so it can sit as a local commit while the sync feature runs as its own single-step cycle. The published bookmark `agent-filesproposal-v028` is still at `main` and can wait or be recreated.
- **One wrinkle:** the three new Todo entries (look-only mode, `zDOING.md`, the rename) exist only in that parked working copy. The feature cycle needs the look-only entry, so those entries would move into its commit, and the parked change would need a small `TODO.md` reconcile when it comes back.
- **Version numbers:** the feature cycle would take 0.84.21 and the agent-files cycle 0.84.22. The agent-files version stays v0.2.8.
- **The alternative** is one multi-step cycle with the feature as a rung ahead of the rule. It avoids the parking but is four commits, and you wanted fewer steps.

**On dry-run as the default**

I'd keep sync acting by default and add `--dry-run` as a flag.
- **Convention:** the project is already split. The repair commands (`fix-desc`, `fix-todo`, `agent-files size`) default to dry-run with `--no-dry-run`. The action commands (`push`, `clone`, `init`) act by default with `--dry-run`. Sync is an action command, typed often.
- **Daily cost:** a dry-run default makes every real sync a longer command, and it would be the second breaking change to `sync` in a row, after the bare-sync change that just landed.
- **The agent doesn't need it:** the rule names the exact flags either way, so the default only affects what you type.

**On a `.vc-config` default**

I'd not add one. A config default makes the bare command mean different things in different workspaces, so the agent-files could never rely on it. The tool's own help makes the same argument for `--allow-jj-mismatch`: "a key gets set once during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing."

**A middle option worth considering**

The risky part of a sync is the automatic rebase of a diverged `main`, not the fast-forward. Sync could keep fast-forwarding by default but stop and report on diverged unless told to rebase. That gets most of the safety of a dry-run default without changing the common case, and `--dry-run` would still exist for the pure look.

The plain version: build `--dry-run` first as its own small cycle, keep sync acting by default, skip the config key, and consider making the diverged rebase opt-in. Then the fetch rule lands once, pointing at `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run`.

1	//! The `sync` subcommand: fetch + classify + rebase / fast-forward
2	//! a workspace's repos against their remotes, then reposition `@`
3	//! onto the synced bookmark.
4	//!
5	//! `--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot
6	//! repo is a linear journal on `main` by design, so every
7	//! per-repo step (tracking preflight, classify, act, reposition)
8	//! resolves its bookmark via `repo_bookmark`, which pins the
9	//! bot repo to `main`.
10	//!
11	//! Sync is a single atomic operation: verify-then-act happens
12	//! inside one invocation against one fetch snapshot (a separate
13	//! check-then-apply pair of runs would race the remote).
14	//!
15	//! **Stop-on-error**: a failure leaves state where the failing step
16	//! stopped so the user can inspect it. Each repo's pre-sync op id
17	//! is captured in memory (`jj::current_op_id`) and the error report
18	//! prints it with the explicit `jj op restore <op> -R <repo>` undo.
19	//! Nothing persists across invocations: a stale snapshot adopted
20	//! later is how the push state file corrupted published history
21	//! (bugs.md #8), so sync keeps none.
22	
23	use std::io::IsTerminal;
24	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
25	
26	use clap::Args;
27	use log::{LevelFilter, debug, info, warn};
28	
29	use crate::common::{prompt, resolve_repos};
30	use crate::context::Context;
31	use crate::jj;
32	use crate::options_flags::scope::{Scope, parse_scope};
33	use crate::subcommand::SubcommandRunner;
34	
35	/// Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.
36	///
37	/// One atomic operation: fetch, classify, fast-forward / rebase the
38	/// bookmark as needed, then reposition `@` onto it. On any failure
39	/// the starting state of every repo is restored via `jj op restore`.
40	///
41	/// Repo set is resolved from `-R/--repo` + `--scope`:
42	///
43	/// - `-R PATH`: workspace root, or a single repo to sync alone.
44	/// - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent`: keyword role selection,
45	///   resolved via the workspace root's `.vc-config.toml`.
46	/// - Neither: `.`, the one repo the command is run in, whichever
47	///   side of a workspace that is, with no walk up from a
48	///   subdirectory. Both repos are asked for with `--scope=both`.
49	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
50	pub struct SyncArgs {
51	    /// Suppress all informational output (exit code signals result)
52	    #[arg(short, long)]
53	    pub quiet: bool,
54	
55	    /// Bookmark to sync in the work repo. The session (bot) repo
56	    /// is a linear journal and always syncs `main`, regardless.
57	    #[arg(long, default_value = "main")]
58	    pub bookmark: String,
59	
60	    /// Remote to sync against
61	    #[arg(long, default_value = "origin")]
62	    pub remote: String,
63	
64	    /// Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without asking.
65	    ///
66	    /// After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
67	    /// bookmark. When the work repo's `@` carries changes it normally
68	    /// asks before rebasing, and `--rebase` answers yes up front for
69	    /// non-interactive use. Ignored for the bot repo (which
70	    /// always `jj new main`).
71	    #[arg(long)]
72	    pub rebase: bool,
73	
74	    /// Workspace root, or a single jj repo to sync on its own.
75	    ///
76	    /// - `-R PATH` alone: sync just the repo at PATH.
77	    /// - `-R PATH -s ROLES`: use PATH as the workspace root and
78	    ///   sync the named side(s).
79	    #[arg(short = 'R', long = "repo", value_name = "PATH", verbatim_doc_comment)]
80	    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,
81	
82	    /// Which repo(s) of the workspace to sync.
83	    ///
84	    /// `SCOPE=work|agent|both`:
85	    ///
86	    /// - `work`: sync only the work repo.
87	    /// - `agent`: sync only the bot repo (errors if no bot repo
88	    ///   is configured).
89	    /// - `both` (or `work,agent`): sync both repos.
90	    ///
91	    /// Composes with `-R` as the workspace root. With neither,
92	    /// sync acts on `.`, the one repo it is run in.
93	    #[arg(
94	        short = 's',
95	        long,
96	        value_name = "SCOPE",
97	        value_parser = parse_scope,
98	        verbatim_doc_comment
99	    )]
100	    pub scope: Option<Scope>,
101	}
102	
103	/// Inputs to the sync op, flat, owned, clap-free.
104	///
105	/// - `quiet`: `-q` / `--quiet`, clamp output to `Warn` for the run.
106	/// - `bookmark`: bookmark to sync in the work repo (default
107	///   `main`). The bot repo always syncs `main`.
108	/// - `remote`: remote to sync against (default `origin`).
109	/// - `rebase`: `--rebase`, rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced
110	///   bookmark without prompting (work repo only, see
111	///   `reposition_work`).
112	/// - `repo`: `-R/--repo` path (None => discover the workspace
113	///   root from cwd).
114	/// - `scope`: `--scope` parsed (None => `.`, unless `repo` names
115	///   a path).
116	pub struct SyncParams {
117	    pub quiet: bool,
118	    pub bookmark: String,
119	    pub remote: String,
120	    pub rebase: bool,
121	    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,
122	    pub scope: Option<Scope>,
123	}
124	
125	impl From<&SyncArgs> for SyncParams {
126	    /// Convert clap-derived `SyncArgs` into the flat `SyncParams`
127	    /// (total: every field copies straight over).
128	    fn from(a: &SyncArgs) -> Self {
129	        Self {
130	            quiet: a.quiet,
131	            bookmark: a.bookmark.clone(),
132	            remote: a.remote.clone(),
133	            rebase: a.rebase,
134	            repo: a.repo.clone(),
135	            scope: a.scope.clone(),
136	        }
137	    }
138	}
139	
140	impl SubcommandRunner for SyncArgs {
141	    type Params = SyncParams;
142	
143	    /// Delegate to the existing `From<&SyncArgs>` impl above
144	    /// (total: never fails).
145	    fn to_params(&self) -> Result<Self::Params, String> {
146	        Ok(SyncParams::from(self))
147	    }
148	
149	    /// Run the existing `sync` op.
150	    fn run(ctx: &mut Context, params: &Self::Params) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
151	        sync(ctx, params)
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	/// Relationship between a local bookmark and its remote counterpart.
156	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
157	pub enum State {
158	    /// Local and remote point at the same commit.
159	    UpToDate,
160	    /// Local is a strict ancestor of remote: fast-forward possible.
161	    Behind { local: String, remote: String },
162	    /// Remote is a strict ancestor of local: nothing to pull in.
163	    Ahead { local: String, remote: String },
164	    /// Neither is an ancestor of the other: needs rebase.
165	    Diverged { local: String, remote: String },
166	    /// The bookmark has no `@<remote>` counterpart.
167	    NoRemote,
168	}
169	
170	/// Per-repo context accumulated between the snapshot and action phases.
171	#[derive(Debug)]
172	struct RepoCtx {
173	    path: PathBuf,
174	    #[allow(dead_code)]
175	    op_id: String,
176	    state: State,
177	}
178	
179	/// CLI entry point for the `sync` subcommand.
180	///
181	/// Thin wrapper over `sync_repos` that resolves `--scope` into a
182	/// concrete repo list (`.` with neither flag, by the resolver the
183	/// read commands share) and forwards the rest. Tests call `sync_repos` directly
184	/// with absolute fixture paths. `ctx` supplies the repo sessions
185	/// the fetch and fast-forward verbs run on (`Context::session`).
186	///
187	/// When `--quiet` is set, the global log filter is temporarily
188	/// clamped to `Warn` for the duration of the call and restored on
189	/// return, so `info!` calls throughout sync (plus any
190	/// subprocess-stderr routed through `common::run`) go dark. Errors
191	/// still surface at `Warn` / `Error` so script callers don't lose
192	/// diagnostics.
193	pub fn sync(ctx: &mut Context, params: &SyncParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
194	    let repos = resolve_repos(params.repo.as_deref(), params.scope.as_ref())?;
195	    if params.quiet {
196	        let prev = log::max_level();
197	        log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Warn);
198	        let result = sync_repos(ctx, &repos, params);
199	        log::set_max_level(prev);
200	        result
201	    } else {
202	        sync_repos(ctx, &repos, params)
203	    }
204	}
205	
206	/// Sync the given repos against their remotes.
207	///
208	/// Orchestrates the full flow: pre-flight clean-check on every repo,
209	/// snapshot each repo's current op id in memory, then hand off to
210	/// `run_plan` for fetch + classify + act, then reposition `@`.
211	///
212	/// **Stop-on-error**: a failure leaves every repo exactly where the
213	/// failing step stopped so the user can inspect what happened:
214	/// nothing is auto-reverted. The error report names each repo's
215	/// pre-sync op id with the explicit `jj op restore` undo. The
216	/// snapshots die with the invocation.
217	///
218	/// Paths may be relative (resolved against the process cwd) or
219	/// absolute. Tests use absolute tempdir paths to avoid cwd dependence
220	/// under parallel `cargo test`.
221	pub fn sync_repos(
222	    ctx: &mut Context,
223	    repos: &[PathBuf],
224	    params: &SyncParams,
225	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
226	    debug!(
227	        "sync: enter (bookmark={}, remote={})",
228	        params.bookmark, params.remote
229	    );
230	
231	    // Preflight: verify bookmark tracking on every repo before any
232	    // fetch/rebase. Implements "Non-tracking-remote bookmark detection",
233	    // design at:
234	    //   https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-06.md#non-tracking-remote-bookmark-detection-design
235	    for repo in repos {
236	        let bookmark = repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark);
237	        if bookmark != params.bookmark {
238	            info!(
239	                "{}: bot repo, syncing 'main' ('{}' is a work repo bookmark)",
240	                repo.display(),
241	                params.bookmark
242	            );
243	        }
244	        crate::common::verify_tracking(repo, bookmark)?;
245	    }
246	
247	    // In-memory only: the snapshot exists to be printed by this
248	    // invocation's failure report, never persisted for a later one.
249	    let mut snapshots: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> = Vec::new();
250	    for repo in repos {
251	        let op_id = jj::current_op_id(repo)?;
252	        debug!("{}: op snapshot = {op_id}", repo.display());
253	        snapshots.push((repo.clone(), op_id));
254	    }
255	
256	    // Run the plan, then reposition `@` onto the freshly-synced
257	    // bookmark. Both live inside the same stop-on-error region: any
258	    // failure falls through to the report below with state left in
259	    // place.
260	    let result = run_plan(ctx, &snapshots, params).and_then(|()| {
261	        for (repo, _) in &snapshots {
262	            reposition_at(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), params)?;
263	        }
264	        Ok(())
265	    });
266	
267	    if let Err(e) = &result {
268	        warn!("sync failed: {e}");
269	        warn!("stopping: state left as-is for inspection (no auto-revert)");
270	        warn!("pre-sync op snapshot per repo:");
271	        for (repo, op_id) in &snapshots {
272	            warn!("  {}: op {op_id}", repo.display());
273	        }
274	        warn!("undo per repo: jj op restore <op> -R <repo>");
275	        debug!("sync: exit");
276	        return result;
277	    }
278	
279	    debug!("sync: exit");
280	    Ok(())
281	}
282	
283	/// Clean-case summary tail ("<N> repo(s) ..." prefixed at the emit
284	/// site). Shared with main.rs's `long_about` so the documented
285	/// output shape can't drift from the emitted one.
286	pub const UP_TO_DATE_MSG: &str = "up to date, nothing to sync";
287	
288	/// Fetch and classify each repo, then act (or not, in verify-only).
289	///
290	/// Returns `Err` on the first failure so the caller can stop and
291	/// report. Partial progress across repos is left in place for
292	/// inspection (see `sync_repos`).
293	fn run_plan(
294	    ctx: &mut Context,
295	    snapshots: &[(PathBuf, String)],
296	    params: &SyncParams,
297	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
298	    // Phase 1: fetch + classify silently.
299	    //
300	    // Each repo's fetch stderr is captured (rather than streamed to
301	    // `info!` via `common::run`) so we can decide after classification
302	    // whether to surface it. `jj git fetch`'s routine "Nothing
303	    // changed." chatter is the main thing we're suppressing here:
304	    // if nothing needs action, the user shouldn't see it.
305	    let mut fetched: Vec<(PathBuf, Vec<String>)> = Vec::new();
306	    let mut ctxs: Vec<RepoCtx> = Vec::new();
307	    for (repo, op_id) in snapshots {
308	        let lines = fetch_silent(ctx, repo, &params.remote)?;
309	        fetched.push((repo.clone(), lines));
310	        let state = classify(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), &params.remote)?;
311	        ctxs.push(RepoCtx {
312	            path: repo.clone(),
313	            op_id: op_id.clone(),
314	            state,
315	        });
316	    }
317	
318	    let any_action_needed = ctxs
319	        .iter()
320	        .any(|c| matches!(c.state, State::Behind { .. } | State::Diverged { .. }));
321	
322	    // Phase 2: emit status. `--quiet` is enforced globally via the
323	    // log-level clamp in `sync()`, so these `info!` calls are already
324	    // suppressed in scripts. We just shape the output here.
325	    if !any_action_needed {
326	        let n = ctxs.len();
327	        let noun = if n == 1 { "repo is" } else { "repos are" };
328	        info!("sync: {n} {noun} {UP_TO_DATE_MSG}");
329	    } else {
330	        for (repo, lines) in &fetched {
331	            info!("{}: fetch {}", repo.display(), params.remote);
332	            for line in lines {
333	                info!("{line}");
334	            }
335	        }
336	        for ctx in &ctxs {
337	            log_state(&ctx.path, &ctx.state);
338	        }
339	    }
340	
341	    // Phase 3: act. Repositioning `@` onto the synced bookmark
342	    // happens after `run_plan` returns (see `sync_repos`), outside
343	    // the revert region.
344	    for repo_ctx in &ctxs {
345	        act_on_state(ctx, repo_ctx, params)?;
346	    }
347	
348	    Ok(())
349	}
350

352	///
353	/// The facade's fetch returns one line per changed remote
354	/// bookmark. The caller decides whether to surface them (action
355	/// case) or drop them (clean case).
356	fn fetch_silent(
357	    ctx: &mut Context,
358	    repo: &Path,
359	    remote: &str,
360	) -> Result<Vec<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {

content.text:
I checked the one thing I was unsure of, and it changes the design: a jj fetch is not a pure look. Tested in scratch repos:

- **Behind:** `jj git fetch` moves the local `main` forward to the remote's by itself. `@` stays on the old commit.
- **Diverged:** `jj git fetch` leaves the local `main` conflicted, pointing at both the local and the remote commit.

So today's acquaint fetch already changes a repo that is behind or diverged, and the rationale's "the fetch moves no local bookmark" is wrong. The parked v0.2.8 already rewrites that sentence, so it gets corrected there.

## Design: one single-step cycle

**Title:** `feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged`

**1. Sync remembers where each bookmark was before the fetch.**
Both new behaviours need this: the pre-fetch position is what "as found" means, and it is the only honest basis for saying behind or diverged, since after the fetch a behind repo already reads as up to date.

**2. `--dry-run`: look only.**
- It fetches, compares each bookmark's pre-fetch position with the remote's, and prints the state and what a sync would do: up to date, would fast-forward, ahead, or diverged and would rebase.
- It then puts any bookmark the fetch moved or conflicted back where it was. `@` is never touched.
- What does change: the remote-tracking refs (`main@origin`), which is the point of looking.
- It honours `--bookmark`, so the acquaint can later look at a cycle bookmark the same way.

**3. Diverged is not rebased unless told.**
- With `--rebase`, sync rebases as it does today. The flag already means "rebase without asking" for a non-empty `@`, so I'd widen it to cover this rather than add a second flag.
- On a terminal without the flag, it asks y/N, as it does for `@`.
- Otherwise it puts the bookmark back on the local commit, reports diverged, and carries on with the other repos.
- Behind still fast-forwards with no question.

**What else the commit carries**
- Tests for each case, the help text, and the README's `sync` section.
- A `BREAKING-CHANGE:` trailer, since a diverged bookmark was rebased automatically before.
- The manifest goes to 0.84.21. No agent-file changes, so the agent-files version stays put.
- `TODO.md`: the two entries now only in the parked change (`zDOING.md` and the `zTODO.md` rename) come along so they reach `main`, and the look-only entry becomes this cycle's block.

## Decisions for you

1. **Exit status when a diverged repo is left alone:** I recommend non-zero, since the sync did not sync, and `--quiet` callers only have the exit code. The alternative is zero with a printed finding.
2. **Exit status of `--dry-run`:** I recommend zero whenever the look itself succeeded, with the states in the output. The alternative is non-zero when anything is not level, like a `--check` flag.
3. **Bookmark:** may I create and publish `feat-sync-can-look-only-and-asks-on-diverged` at `main`? That is a push, so it needs your go.

The plain version: sync gets a `--dry-run` that reports and leaves the local bookmark and `@` where they were, and a real sync stops rebasing a diverged `main` unless you pass `--rebase` or say yes. It is one commit, then v0.2.8 comes back and points the rules at `--dry-run`.

1246	| diverged | neither is ancestor | `jj rebase -b <local-head> -d <b>@<remote>` |

1254	pass, run after every repo syncs cleanly. The rule differs by repo (`@-` is the parent of `@`, `<b>`

### sync

Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes in one atomic operation: fetch, converge the
bookmark, reposition `@`. With no flags the repo set is `.`, the one repo `sync` is run in, whichever
side of a workspace that is. Name a side or both with `-s` / `--scope`, or point at a different
workspace root or single repo with `-R` / `--repo`. There are no modes: verify-then-act happens inside a single invocation against one fetch
snapshot (a separate check-then-apply pair of runs would race the remote).

Per repo, `sync` classifies the local bookmark against its remote:

| State | Meaning | Action |
|------|---------|--------|
| up-to-date | local == remote | none |
| behind | local is ancestor of remote | `jj bookmark set <b> -r <b>@<remote>` |
| ahead | remote is ancestor of local | none (push is a separate step) |
| diverged | neither is ancestor | `jj rebase -b <local-head> -d <b>@<remote>` |
| no remote | bookmark has no `@<remote>` counterpart | none, skip |

`--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot repo is a linear journal on `main` by
design, so its side of every step (tracking preflight, classify, act, reposition) always uses `main`
regardless of the flag.

After the bookmark action above, `sync` repositions `@` onto the freshly-synced bookmark as a final
pass, run after every repo syncs cleanly. The rule differs by repo (`@-` is the parent of `@`, `<b>`
is the synced `--bookmark`):

- **Work repo** (the workspace root):
  - `@` is clean (empty) and `<b>` sits ahead of `@-` on the same line -> `jj new <b>` starts a
    fresh `@` on the new tip (the old empty `@` is auto-abandoned).
  - `@` has changes -> `sync` asks before moving it, and `--rebase` answers yes up front (`jj
    rebase -b @ -d <b>`). Declining, or not being a TTY with no `--rebase`, leaves `@` in place and
    says so.
  - `@` already sits on `<b>`, or `<b>` isn't on `@-`'s line (diverged / `@` ahead) -> `@` is left
    untouched, with a note why.
- **Bot repo** (`.claude`): no-op when `@-` is already the `main` tip, so `@` keeps its change id
  and any live session writes stay in the working copy. When `main` moved, `jj new main` starts a
  fresh empty `@` on the new tip, and the prior `@` (e.g. `/exit`'s trailing session writes) is
  preserved as a sibling head. If `@-` isn't on `main`, `sync` errors rather than strand it.

On any failure during fetch/classify/act/reposition (conflicted rebase, subprocess error, anything)
`sync` **stops where the failing step stopped**. Nothing is auto-reverted, so the state can be
inspected as-is (jj's operation log holds everything, so nothing is lost by stopping). Before
acting, sync captures each repo's pre-sync `jj op` id in memory, and the failure report lists
every repo's op id. The undo is explicit, per repo: `jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing
persists across
invocations: a snapshot that outlives its run is a stale target waiting to rewind unrelated work.
That is also why the former `revert` subcommand was removed at 0.78.3: it restored the persisted
snapshot with no guard against discarding operations recorded after the failed sync. A safer
revert would derive its target from the op log and refuse when unrelated operations sit in
between. Until such a design exists, `jj op log` + `jj op restore` is the recovery.

```
vc-x1 sync                            # the repo in the current directory
vc-x1 sync --rebase                   # rebase a dirty @ onto the bookmark without asking
vc-x1 sync --scope=work               # only the work repo
vc-x1 sync --scope=agent              # only the agent repo
vc-x1 sync --scope=both               # both repos of a dual workspace
vc-x1 sync -R ../other                # sync ../other as a single repo
vc-x1 sync -R ../other --scope=work,bot   # ../other as workspace root
```

**Repo set resolution.** `-R` and `--scope` compose:

1. Neither: `.`, the one repo in the current directory, as `chid`, `desc`, `list`, and `show` take
   no flags. There is no walk up, so from a subdirectory of a repo `sync` fails with "There is no
   Jujutsu repo in ." and changes nothing.
2. `-R PATH` alone: sync just the repo at `PATH`.
3. `--scope=work|bot|work,bot` alone: workspace roles, resolved via the discovered workspace root's
   `.vc-config.md` (`work` -> root, `agent` -> the root-joined `agent` path).
4. `-R PATH --scope=ROLES`: roles resolved against `PATH` as the workspace root.

A named scope is cwd-portable: from the agent repo's directory, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both` walks up
to the workspace root and resolves both repos by absolute path. A bare `vc-x1 sync` there syncs the
agent repo alone.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Workspace root, or a single repo to sync alone. Composes with `--scope` |

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done and what was just done: the running cycle's planning and its work's
documentation, and the last finished cycle's. What we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), with one difference
on trial: the Ladder comes ahead of the Deliberation.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## In Progress

### feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged

#### Problem

A `vc-x1 sync` fetches and then acts, and it has no way to look without acting. A repo that is
behind is fast-forwarded and one that diverged is rebased, with no question asked, so a session
that only wants to know whether its repos are level, as an acquaint and a cycle start do, cannot
ask `sync` and reads the state by hand after a `jj git fetch`. That fetch is not a look either: it
moves a tracked bookmark that is behind and leaves one that diverged conflicted.

#### Solution

Sync reads where each bookmark is before it fetches, and classifies and reports from that. A
`--dry-run` flag makes the run a look: it fetches, reports each repo's state and what a sync would
do, puts back any bookmark the fetch moved, and touches no `@`. A real sync rebases a diverged
bookmark only on a go, `--rebase` or a yes at the prompt, and otherwise leaves it as found and
fails the run naming it.

#### Acceptance check

- In a scratch clone that is behind its remote, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports behind and leaves
  `main` and `@` where they were, and a `vc-x1 sync` after it fast-forwards.
- In a scratch clone that diverged, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports diverged and leaves `main` on
  the local commit, not conflicted. A `vc-x1 sync` there exits non-zero naming the repo and
  leaves `main` the same, and `vc-x1 sync --rebase` rebases it.
- In this workspace, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run` reports both repos up to date.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged (current)

#### Deliberation

- The record is in this file: a trial, on wink's word, of the planning and the work's
  documentation living apart from the backlog.
  - It bends [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record), which names `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. The
    bend covers where this cycle's block is written and nothing else: every other step of the
    protocol runs as the agent-files say.
  - `## Continuation notes` stays in `TODO.md` for now, since [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)
    reads it there, and `TODO.md` keeps its `## In Progress` and `## Closed` headings, each
    pointing here.
  - The Ladder is ahead of the Deliberation, the order wink wants, also ahead of the rule.
- This cycle runs before agent-files v0.2.8, which is parked on its bookmark: its rule, "every
  cycle start syncs", is to name `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run`, and a rule written against
  the acting sync would be rewritten a cycle later.
- A fetch is not a look, found by trial in scratch repos: `jj git fetch` moves a tracked `main`
  that is behind to the remote's, and leaves one that diverged conflicted.
  - So the state is classified from the bookmark as it was before the fetch. Classified after,
    a repo that was behind reads as up to date.
  - A look puts the bookmark back with a `bookmark set`, not a `jj op restore` to the pre-fetch
    operation: the restore would also take back the remote-tracking refs, which are what the look
    is for, and it would rewind whatever the fetch's own snapshot of a live `@` recorded.
- `--dry-run` is the flag, and acting stays the default, wink's call.
  - The repair commands, `fix-desc`, `fix-todo`, and `agent-files size`, default to a dry run. The
    action commands, `push`, `clone`, and `init`, act and take `--dry-run`, and `sync` is one of
    those.
  - No `.vc-config` key sets the default: a bare command that means different things in different
    workspaces is one no rule can name.
- Diverged is rebased only on a go, the "middle option" wink chose over a dry-run default: the
  rebase is the risky act, and a fast-forward loses nothing.
  - The go is `--rebase`, widened from "rebase a non-empty `@` without asking" to both rebases, in
    place of a second flag.
  - With no go the run still syncs the other repos, then exits non-zero: the repo was not synced,
    and a `--quiet` caller has only the exit status to learn that from.
  - It is a breaking change, and a patch, no minor having been named.
- A look exits 0 whatever it found. The states are in the output, and a look that worked is not a
  failure. The other choice, non-zero when a repo is not level, is what a `--check` flag would
  mean, and those flags were retired from `sync` once already.
- An ahead bookmark is reported, where it was folded into "up to date, nothing to sync": an
  unpushed `main` is one of the findings an acquaint reports.
- Single-step: one flag, one changed default, and the classification both rest on.
- Two Todo entries came along from the parked change so they reach `main`: the reworked
  `zDOING.md` entry and [TODO.md is renamed zTODO.md](TODO.md#todomd-is-renamed-ztodomd).
- The `## Waiting` entry's condition is unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed, so nothing promotes.

opening.

Yes, that is the model, and it is simpler than what the agent-files say today:

1. Pick a Todo in `TODO.md` and move it, whole, into `zDOING.md`.
2. Everything about the cycle from then on is written there, under that Todo: the deliberation, the plan, the ladder and the per-rung details.
3. When the cycle closes, the block moves to `## Closed` in the same file, and the next cycle replaces it.

`TODO.md` only ever holds what we might do.

The current `zDOING.md` differs from that in two places, and I'd like to fix both before going on:

- **The sync block does not start with its Todo.** I wrote a fresh Problem and Solution, because the look-only Todo entry only existed in the parked v0.2.8 change. I'd put that entry's text at the top of the block, as picked, and cut my Problem down so it doesn't repeat it.

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done and what was just done: the running cycle's planning and its work's
documentation, and the last finished cycle's. What we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
plan, Solution and Acceptance check, then the Ladder and its details, and the Deliberation last.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## In Progress

### feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged

(wink, 2026-10-09) A `vc-x1 sync` fetches and then acts: a `main` that is behind is fast-forwarded,
one that diverged is rebased, and `@` is repositioned. An acquaint and a cycle start want to report
a repo as found before anything moves, which today takes a `jj git fetch` and a look.

- A `--dry-run` flag, as `push`, `clone`, and `init` have: the sync fetches, prints each repo's
  state and what a sync would do, and moves no bookmark and no `@`.
- The fetch still runs, since the remote's state is what is being looked at, and it changes only
  the remote-tracking refs.
- A sync is cautious on diverged: it rebases only when told to.
- The parked agent-files v0.2.8 follows it, pointing its two steps at the flag.

#### Solution

Sync reads where each bookmark is before it fetches, and classifies and reports from that. A
`--dry-run` flag makes the run a look: it fetches, reports each repo's state and what a sync would
do, puts back any bookmark the fetch moved, and touches no `@`. A real sync rebases a diverged
bookmark only on a go, `--rebase` or a yes at the prompt, and otherwise leaves it as found and
fails the run naming it.

#### Acceptance check

- In a scratch clone that is behind its remote, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports behind and leaves
  `main` and `@` where they were, and a `vc-x1 sync` after it fast-forwards.
- In a scratch clone that diverged, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports diverged and leaves `main` on
  the local commit, not conflicted. A `vc-x1 sync` there exits non-zero naming the repo and
  leaves `main` the same, and `vc-x1 sync --rebase` rebases it.
- In this workspace, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run` reports both repos up to date.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged (current)

""")

file.content:
**Output shape.** Sync collapses output based on what it finds:

- **All up-to-date**: one-line summary, `sync: N repos are up to date, nothing to sync`. Nothing
  else (no-op reposition lines are debug-level). Makes "sprinkle sync everywhere" genuinely cheap.
  Scope is bookmark-vs-remote tracking, `@` may have uncommitted working-copy changes, and sync
  intentionally doesn't speak to that (use `jj st` for working-copy state).
- **Action needed** (`behind` / `diverged`): per-repo fetch + state lines, then the actions run.
- **`--quiet`**: no output at any level, and the exit code is the only signal. Intended for
  scripts that just need success/failure.

**Note on the `behind` case.** jj's `git fetch` already fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark when
it's a strict ancestor of the incoming remote, so in the common case `sync` reports `up-to-date`
rather than `behind`. The `behind` branch covers untracked bookmarks and edge configs where
auto-advance is disabled.

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("README.md"); s = p.read_text()
def rep(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, (s.count(old), old[:60])
    s = s.replace(old, new)

rep("""side of a workspace that is. Name a side or both with `-s` / `--scope`, or point at a different
workspace root or single repo with `-R` / `--repo`. There are no modes: verify-then-act happens inside a single invocation against one fetch
snapshot (a separate check-then-apply pair of runs would race the remote).

Per repo, `sync` classifies the local bookmark against its remote:
""", """side of a workspace that is. Name a side or both with `-s` / `--scope`, or point at a different
workspace root or single repo with `-R` / `--repo`. Verify-then-act happens inside a single
invocation against one fetch snapshot, since a separate check-then-apply pair of runs would race
the remote. A look with `--dry-run` is not that check: a sync after it verifies again.

Per repo, `sync` classifies the local bookmark, as it was before the fetch, against its remote:
""")
rep("""| diverged | neither is ancestor | `jj rebase -b <local-head> -d <b>@<remote>` |
""", """| diverged | neither is ancestor | on a go, `jj rebase -b <local-head> -d <b>@<remote>` |
""")
rep("""`--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot repo is a linear journal on `main` by
design,""", """The bookmark is read before the fetch because the fetch is not a look: jj's `git fetch` moves a
tracked bookmark that is behind to the remote's, and leaves one that diverged conflicted. Where the
bookmark was is what "as found" means, and two paths put it back there:

- **`--dry-run`** looks only. It fetches, reports each repo's state and what a sync would do, and
  moves no bookmark and no `@`. The remote-tracking refs (`<b>@<remote>`) are what it updates. It
  exits 0 whenever the look itself succeeded, whatever it found.
- **A diverged bookmark is rebased only on a go**: `--rebase`, or a yes at the prompt on a
  terminal. With neither, the bookmark is left as found, the other repos still sync, and the run
  then exits non-zero naming the repo, so a `--quiet` caller learns it was not synced.

`--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot repo is a linear journal on `main` by
design,""")
rep("""vc-x1 sync --rebase                   # rebase a dirty @ onto the bookmark without asking
""", """vc-x1 sync --dry-run                  # look only: report, and move nothing
vc-x1 sync --rebase                   # rebase a diverged bookmark or a dirty @ without asking
""")
rep("""| `--rebase` | Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without prompting (work repo only) |
""", """| `--rebase` | Rebase without prompting: a diverged bookmark onto its remote, and a non-empty work repo `@` onto the synced bookmark |
| `--dry-run` | Look only: fetch and report, moving no bookmark and no `@` |
""")
rep("""- **Action needed** (`behind` / `diverged`): per-repo fetch + state lines, then the actions run.
""", """- **Anything else** (`behind` / `ahead` / `diverged`): per-repo fetch + state lines, then the
  actions run, or with `--dry-run` what a sync would do.
""")
rep("""**Note on the `behind` case.** jj's `git fetch` already fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark when
it's a strict ancestor of the incoming remote, so in the common case `sync` reports `up-to-date`
rather than `behind`. The `behind` branch covers untracked bookmarks and edge configs where
auto-advance is disabled.""", """**Note on the `behind` case.** jj's `git fetch` already fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark when
it's a strict ancestor of the incoming remote. Sync reports `behind` all the same, since it
classifies from where the bookmark was before the fetch, and its own `bookmark set` then covers
untracked bookmarks and edge configs where auto-advance is disabled.""")
p.write_text(s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance check for `feat: sync can look only, and asks on diverged`.
# b is a clone left behind its remote, c one that diverged.
set -uo pipefail
d="$1"
rm -rf "$d"
mkdir -p "$d"
cd "$d" || exit 1
git init -q --bare remote.git
jj git clone --quiet remote.git a
(cd a && echo one > f && jj commit --quiet -m one && jj bookmark set --quiet main -r @- \
  && jj git push --quiet --bookmark main)
jj git clone --quiet remote.git b
jj git clone --quiet remote.git c
(cd a && echo two > g && jj commit --quiet -m two && jj bookmark set --quiet main -r @- \
  && jj git push --quiet --bookmark main)
(cd c && echo local > h && jj commit --quiet -m local && jj bookmark set --quiet main -r @-)

show() { jj log -R "$1" -r 'main | @- | main@origin' --no-graph \
  -T 'commit_id.short(8) ++ " " ++ bookmarks ++ " " ++ remote_bookmarks ++ " | " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"'; }

echo "=== behind: before"; show b
echo "=== behind: sync --dry-run"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R b --dry-run; echo "exit=$?"; show b
echo "=== behind: sync"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R b; echo "exit=$?"; show b

echo "=== diverged: before"; show c
echo "=== diverged: sync --dry-run"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R c --dry-run; echo "exit=$?"; show c
echo "=== diverged: sync (no go, no terminal)"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R c < /dev/null; echo "exit=$?"; show c
echo "=== diverged: sync --rebase"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R c --rebase; echo "exit=$?"; show c

A sync, `vc-x1 sync`, fetches and then acts, with no way to only look:
a bookmark that is behind is fast-forwarded and one that diverged is
rebased, unasked. To "look only" is to fetch, report, and move
nothing, and to "ask on diverged" is to rebase only when told.

    sync would do, and moves no bookmark and no `@`. It exits 0
    whenever the look itself succeeded.

  and leaves one that diverged conflicted.
  - Sync reads each bookmark before the fetch and classifies from
    that, so a repo that was behind is reported as behind.
  - A look puts back any bookmark the fetch moved.
* A diverged bookmark is rebased with no question.
  - It is rebased only on a go, --rebase or a yes at the prompt. With
    neither it is put back as found, the other repos still sync, and
    the run then fails naming it.
* An ahead bookmark is reported as up to date.
  - It is reported as ahead, in the per-repo lines.

BREAKING-CHANGE: `vc-x1 sync` no longer rebases a diverged bookmark
unasked. Without --rebase or a yes at the prompt it leaves the
bookmark as found and exits non-zero.
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# What does a fetch do when the remote REWROTE a commit the clone has
# (a forced push, as squash-push makes)? b holds work in @ on top of it.
set -uo pipefail
d="$1"
rm -rf "$d"
mkdir -p "$d"
cd "$d" || exit 1
git init -q --bare remote.git
jj git clone --quiet remote.git a
(cd a && echo one > f && jj commit --quiet -m one && jj bookmark set --quiet main -r @- \
  && jj git push --quiet --bookmark main)
jj git clone --quiet remote.git b
jj git clone --quiet remote.git c
# a rewrites the pushed commit and force-pushes it.
(cd a && jj edit --quiet main && echo rewritten > f && jj new --quiet \
  && jj git push --quiet --bookmark main)
# b has uncommitted work in @ touching the same file.
echo "b-local-edit" > b/f

show() { jj log -R "$1" -r 'all()' --no-graph \
  -T 'commit_id.short(8) ++ " " ++ if(conflict, "CONFLICT ", "") ++ if(current_working_copy, "@ ", "") ++ bookmarks ++ " " ++ remote_bookmarks ++ " | " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"'; }

echo "=== b before"; show b
echo "=== b: sync --dry-run"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R b --dry-run; echo "exit=$?"
show b; echo "--- b/f:"; cat b/f
echo "=== c (clean @) before"; show c
echo "=== c: sync --dry-run"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R c --dry-run; echo "exit=$?"
show c
echo "=== c: sync"; vc-x1-dev --no-banner sync -R c < /dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
show c

lastPrompt: Under what circumstances can there be a conflict on a fetch? If that happens what are we going to do?

content.text:
Good question, and testing it turned up a real hole. Please don't approve the push yet.

**When a fetch can cause a conflict**

There are two different kinds, and I had only handled the first.

1. **A conflicted bookmark.** The local bookmark and the remote's have both moved to different commits since the last fetch. jj leaves the bookmark pointing at both. This is the "diverged" case. It happens when:
   - a commit was made on `main` here and not pushed, and another machine pushed first;
   - two sessions or machines both wrote the agent-repo's `main`.

   No file is touched. This is what the change handles: `--dry-run` and a sync with no go both put the bookmark back.

2. **A file conflict in `@`.** The remote *rewrote* a commit this clone already has, by a forced push. jj sees the old commit as replaced and rebases everything on top of it, including `@`, onto the new version during the fetch. If `@` holds edits to the same lines, the working-copy file ends up with conflict markers. This happens when:
   - `squash-push` amends an already-pushed commit, which is routine for the agent-repo and happens to cycle bookmarks;
   - a cycle bookmark is rebased or amended and force-pushed from another clone.

   It needs a second clone of the same repo, so it does not happen on one machine. A landed work-repo `main` is never rewritten, so that bookmark is safe.

**What I just tested for case 2**

I rewrote a pushed commit from one scratch clone and ran `vc-x1-dev sync --dry-run` in another that had an uncommitted edit to the same file:

- `--dry-run` exited 0 and reported "diverged", but `@` had been moved onto the rewritten commit and the file on disk now held conflict markers.
- My put-back made it worse: it pointed `main` back at the replaced commit while `@` sat on the new one.
- A plain `sync` with no go did the same thing, then exited 1.

So "moves no bookmark and no `@`" is false in this case, and the acceptance check missed it because both of its scenarios were case 1.

**What I recommend we do**

Replace the bookmark put-back with a full undo of the fetch for that repo: snapshot the working copy, note the operation, fetch and classify, report, then restore the repo to that operation. The facade already has this restore and it puts the working copy back too.

- **`--dry-run`:** always restores, so the repo is exactly as found, files included.
- **Sync with no go on diverged:** restores that repo the same way, then fails naming it.
- **Cost:** the remote-tracking refs (`main@origin`) also go back to their old value, so only the printed report tells you what the remote holds. I earlier chose the put-back to keep those refs; that was the wrong trade.
- **Sync with a go:** unchanged. A rebase that produces conflicts still stops with the state in place and prints the operation ids to undo it.

I'd also add this rewritten-remote scenario as a test and to the acceptance check, and report it as "remote rewritten" if I can tell it apart from an ordinary divergence.

Shall I make that change? It stays in this one commit, and I'll bring it back to "please review" when it passes.

content.text:
I think your instinct is right, and jj already has the mechanism you're reaching for. The bookmark idea would work less well than what jj gives us for free.

**Why not bookmarks**
- **We can't know which commits to mark.** When the remote has rewritten a commit, the fetch rebases whatever sits on top of it. That set isn't known until the fetch has run.
- **A bookmark pins a commit, not a state.** Getting back means restoring where every bookmark pointed, where `@` was, and the files on disk. Marker bookmarks record none of that.
- **jj never deletes the old commits anyway.** They stay reachable through the operation log, so a pin adds nothing.

**What jj already has**

Every jj action is recorded as an operation holding the whole repo state: all bookmarks, `@`, and the working copy. `jj op restore <op>` returns the repo to exactly that point. Sync already notes each repo's operation before it starts and prints it when a run fails. The safety net exists; the problem is that sync only tells you about it after a failure, and leaves the mess for you to undo by hand.

**What I'd make the default**

1. **All or nothing.** A sync either ends with the repo cleanly synced, or it puts the repo back exactly as found and says why. Today it stops mid-way "for inspection". Keeping the mess would become the opt-in, for someone who wants to look at it.
2. **Only harmless acts without a go.** Unasked, sync would do just two things: fast-forward a bookmark, and move an empty `@` onto it. Anything else needs `--rebase`: a diverged bookmark, a remote that rewrote history, a `@` holding work that would be rebased. Without the go, the repo is restored and the report says what was found.
3. **A one-word undo.** Something like `vc-x1 sync --undo`, which finds the last sync in the operation log and restores to just before it. It should refuse if other work has happened since, so it can't discard that. Every sync that changed something would end by printing that this exists.

**What that does and doesn't guarantee**
- **It covers everything local:** bookmarks, `@`, files on disk. Sync never pushes, so nothing on the remote is at risk.
- **One gap:** if something else writes the repo during the sync, such as a live agent session in the agent-repo, the restore would take that write back with it. The window is under a second.
- **History to respect:** the old `revert` command was removed at 0.78.3 because it restored a saved snapshot that could be stale. Points 1 and 2 don't have that problem, since the restore happens inside the same run. Point 3 does, which is why it needs the refusal guard, and the README already sketches that design.

**How I'd split the work**
- **This cycle:** points 1 and 2. They replace the put-back I was about to rework anyway, and they are what makes `--dry-run` honest.
- **Its own Todo:** point 3, the undo command. It is a separate design with its own risk.

The plain version: don't mark commits, use jj's operation log. Make sync restore the repo by itself whenever it can't finish cleanly, let it do only fast-forwards unasked, and add a guarded `--undo` later for the case where a sync finished but you wish it hadn't.

content.text:
Either works, and the shape is still free to change because nothing but the bookmark has been pushed. I lean toward making `--undo` the very next cycle rather than a rung, but it's close.

**What a rung costs**
- **Commit count.** With a second step this becomes a multi-step cycle: opening, the all-or-nothing sync, `--undo`, closing. That is four commits where two single-step cycles would be two.
- **It holds up the rest.** The parked v0.2.8 only needs `--dry-run`. With `--undo` as a rung, v0.2.8 and the `zDOING.md` cycle both wait for the undo design to be settled.

**What a rung buys**
- **The safety story lands whole.** Points 1 and 2 protect a sync that can't finish. `--undo` covers the sync that finished but you regret. As one cycle, `main` never has the first without the second.
- **Same code, same context.** It is the same file and the same tests, and the reasoning is fresh.

**Why I'd still separate it: the undo design has open questions**
- **Finding "the last sync".** A sync is several jj operations: a snapshot, the fetch, a bookmark move, a new `@`. Sync would have to mark its operations so `--undo` can find where the run began.
- **The refusal guard.** `--undo` must refuse when other work followed the sync. In the agent-repo a live session writes constantly, so a naive guard would always refuse there.
- **A real hazard in the agent-repo.** Restoring an operation also resets the files on disk to that point. Minutes after a sync, that would overwrite a live session's newer writes. The undo needs to carry the current `@` forward rather than rewind it, which is new logic.

That last point also touches points 1 and 2: the automatic restore has the same hazard for the fraction of a second a sync takes. I'd handle it there by restoring only when the working copy hasn't changed since the sync began, and otherwise stopping as it does today and printing how to undo by hand.

**My recommendation**
- Keep this cycle single-step: points 1 and 2 plus `--dry-run`.
- Put `--undo` first in `TODO.md` and run it as the next cycle, before v0.2.8 resumes if you want the safety story complete before the rules point at sync.

If you would rather see it land as one unit on `main`, a rung is a perfectly good choice; the cost is the two bookend commits and a longer wait for everything behind it.

The plain version: `--undo` is worth doing soon, but it has enough unsettled design that I'd give it its own small cycle right after this one instead of stretching this one to four commits.

content.text:
That's a sound reason, and with nothing pushed it costs only commits. If the cycle's point is "sync can't hurt you", then it isn't finished until a regretted sync can be undone, and landing it as one unit on `main` says that.

How I'd shape it:

**Title.** The cycle is now bigger than "can look only, and asks on diverged". Something like `feat: sync is safe by default` names the whole thing. The published bookmark is still empty at `main`, so I'd delete it and create one from the new title; both are pushes that need your go.

**Ladder, kept to three commits.** The rules allow a cycle to skip the separate opening commit and let its first work commit carry the setup:
1. `feat: sync is all or nothing, and can look only`. This is the work already written, reworked so that sync restores the repo when it can't finish cleanly, does only fast-forwards unasked, and `--dry-run` restores always.
2. `feat: sync --undo takes back the last sync`.
3. `feat: sync is safe by default closing`.

With a separate opening commit it would be four. I'd skip it.

**What needs settling before the `--undo` rung is coded.** I'd write these into `zDOING.md` as the rung's plan and have you review that before any code:
- **How a sync marks its operations**, so `--undo` can find where the last run began.
- **When `--undo` refuses.** My starting point: it refuses if any operation after the sync changed a bookmark or a commit, and it tolerates plain working-copy snapshots, since a live session makes those constantly.
- **What happens to current work in `@`.** It is carried forward onto the restored state, never rewound, so a live session's writes survive.
- **Scope:** one repo or both, following the same `-R` and `--scope` rules as sync.

**Order of work.** Rung 1 first, through review and push, so the reworked restore logic is settled before `--undo` builds on it. The same "carry `@` forward" logic serves both.

**What waits.** The parked v0.2.8 and the `zDOING.md` cycle stay behind this until it lands. v0.2.8 could then also mention `--undo` in its rule if you want.

The plain version: yes, make it one cycle of three commits under a broader title, do the restore rework first, and agree the undo design on paper in `zDOING.md` before I write it.

block = '''## In Progress

### feat: sync is safe by default

(wink, 2026-10-09) A `vc-x1 sync` fetches and then acts: a `main` that is behind is fast-forwarded,
one that diverged is rebased, and `@` is repositioned. An acquaint and a cycle start want to report
a repo as found before anything moves, which today takes a `jj git fetch` and a look.

- A `--dry-run` flag, as `push`, `clone`, and `init` have: the sync fetches, prints each repo's
  state and what a sync would do, and moves no bookmark and no `@`.
- A sync is dangerous enough that its default guarantees, as best it can, that it messes nothing
  up, and that a neophyte can put things back the way they were before it.
- The parked agent-files v0.2.8 follows it, pointing its two steps at the flag.

#### Solution

A sync ends one of two ways for each repo: synced cleanly, or exactly as found with the reason
said. Unasked it does only what loses nothing, a fast-forward and the move of an empty `@`, and
everything else waits for a go. With `--dry-run` it looks and always leaves the repo as found.
With `--undo` it takes back the last sync, for the one that finished and is regretted.

#### Acceptance check

- In a scratch clone that is behind its remote, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports behind and leaves
  the repo as found, and a `vc-x1 sync` after it fast-forwards.
- In a scratch clone that diverged, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` reports it and leaves the repo as
  found, a `vc-x1 sync` exits non-zero naming the repo and leaves it as found, and
  `vc-x1 sync --rebase` rebases it.
- In a scratch clone whose remote rewrote a commit under an edited `@`, `vc-x1 sync --dry-run` and
  `vc-x1 sync` each leave `@`, `main`, and the edited file as found.
- After a `vc-x1 sync` that fast-forwarded, `vc-x1 sync --undo` puts `main` and `@` back, and it
  refuses when a commit was made since.
- In this workspace, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run` reports both repos up to date.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- [feat: sync is all or nothing, and can look only][1] (current)
- [feat: sync --undo takes back the last sync][2]
- [feat: sync is safe by default closing][3]

##### feat: sync is all or nothing, and can look only

A sync that cannot finish cleanly stops where it failed and leaves the repo for inspection, a
diverged bookmark is rebased unasked, and there is no way to only look. The cycle's setup rides in
this commit, there being no separate opening.

- As found is an operation, not a bookmark: before it fetches, sync snapshots the working copy and
  notes the repo's operation, and putting a repo back is a restore to that operation.
- A fetch is not a look. It moves a tracked bookmark that is behind, conflicts one that diverged,
  and, when the remote rewrote a commit the clone has, rebases `@` onto the rewrite and can leave
  conflict markers in a file. So the state is classified from the bookmark as it was before the
  fetch, and a look restores whenever the fetch changed anything.
- Unasked acts: a fast-forward, and the move of an empty `@` onto it. A diverged bookmark and a
  fetch that left a conflict wait for `--rebase` or a yes at the prompt, and with no go the repo
  is restored and the run fails naming it, after the other repos have synced.
- A failed step restores too, where it stopped and kept the state before. `--keep` asks for the
  old behaviour, the state left in place with the operation ids to undo it by hand.
- The restore does not run over a live writer: when the working copy changed while the sync ran,
  the repo is left where it is and the report says how to undo by hand.

##### feat: sync --undo takes back the last sync

A sync that finished cleanly and is regretted has no way back but `jj op restore` and an operation
id read from the log. The design is agreed here before it is written:

- Finding the last sync: to be settled, how a sync marks its operations so `--undo` knows where
  the last run began.
- Refusing: to be settled. The starting point is to refuse when an operation after the sync
  changed a bookmark or a commit, and to tolerate plain working-copy snapshots, which a live
  session makes constantly.
- Work in `@` now: carried forward onto the restored state, never rewound.
- Scope: the repo set `-R` and `--scope` name, as a sync takes them.

##### feat: sync is safe by default closing

Closing out the cycle.

#### Deliberation

- The record is in this file: a trial, on wink's word, of the planning and the work's
  documentation living apart from the backlog.
  - It bends [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record), which names `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. The
    bend covers where this cycle's block is written and its order, and nothing else: every other
    step of the protocol runs as the agent-files say.
  - The block opens with the Todo as picked, then the plan, the Ladder and its details, and the

# Which operations does a sync record? c diverged with a conflicting edit.
set -uo pipefail
bin="$1"
d="$2"

echo "=== ops after"; ops c
